interactions.notes: CORRECTION: the widely repeated 'ginkgo raises INR' claim is not supported - ginkgo does not change INR; any risk is additive platelet inhibition, so caution remains before surgery and with antiplatelets.

interactions.mechanism: Proposed antiplatelet effect (ajoene, inhibits platelet aggregation) -> additive bleeding tendency; no consistent PK change.
interactions.direction: Case reports of raised INR/bleeding; aged garlic extract RCT showed no increased bleeding risk or INR change.
interactions.evidence: case reports (Sunter 1991, Pharm J - not PubMed indexed) + small RCT (negative) + reviews

sources.citation: Macan H et al. Aged garlic extract may be safe for patients on warfarin therapy. J Nutr 2006
Borrelli F et al. Garlic (Allium sativum L.): adverse effects and drug interactions in humans. Mol Nutr Food Res 2007
Sunter WH. Warfarin and garlic. Pharm J 1991;246:722 (not PubMed-indexed)

interactions.notes: CORRECTION: evidence is weak; the 'garlic + warfarin = bleed' claim rests on two old case reports. Perioperative bleeding with high-dose garlic is the more plausible concern.

interactions.mechanism: Induction of intestinal CYP3A4 and/or P-gp (exact mechanism unclear).
interactions.direction: Lowers saquinavir AUC ~51%, trough ~49%, Cmax ~54%; only partially recovered (60-70% of baseline) after 10-day washout.

sources.citation: Piscitelli SC et al. The effect of garlic supplements on the pharmacokinetics of saquinavir. Clin Infect Dis 2002

interactions.notes: Effect is with unboosted saquinavir; ritonavir boosting may override it. Slow offset after stopping is notable.

interactions.mechanism: Curcumin inhibits CYP3A4 and P-gp in vitro (raising tacrolimus); antiplatelet activity and possible CYP2C9 inhibition (warfarin).
interactions.direction: Raises tacrolimus levels (case of toxicity in renal transplant patient eating turmeric/curry); raised INR with vitamin K antagonist (case).
interactions.evidence: case reports + in vitro/animal; one interaction study (Meriva) found no interaction

sources.citation: Boissiere C et al. Spice-drug interactions: a case report on the use of turmeric, curry and ginger in a renal transplant patient on tacrolimus. Eur J Hosp Pharm 2023
Daveluy A et al. Probable interaction between an oral vitamin K antagonist and turmeric (Curcuma longa). Therapie 2014
Hu S et al. Interaction study between antiplatelet agents, anticoagulants, thyroid replacement therapy and a bioavailable formulation of curcumin (Meriva). Eur Rev Med Pharmacol Sci 2018

interactions.notes: Culinary turmeric is very poorly absorbed; risk rises with high-dose and 'enhanced bioavailability' (piperine/phospholipid) supplements. The often-cited Nayeri 2017 tacrolimus case was not confirmed by this search.

interactions.mechanism: Inhibition of hepatic and intestinal glucuronidation (UGT) of curcumin, plus CYP3A4/P-gp inhibition.
interactions.direction: Raises curcumin bioavailability: in humans 2 g curcumin + 20 mg piperine increased bioavailability ~2000% (20-fold) with no adverse effects in that study; in rats ~154%.
interactions.significance: beneficial/intended (but makes curcumin-drug interactions more likely)

sources.citation: Shoba G et al. Influence of piperine on the pharmacokinetics of curcumin in animals and human volunteers. Planta Med 1998

interactions.notes: The '2000%' figure comes from very low baseline levels (curcumin often barely detectable alone); absolute serum levels remained low.

interactions.mechanism: Inhibition of CYP-mediated metabolism (CYP1A2, CYP3A4, CYP2C9) and P-gp; possibly increased absorption.
interactions.direction: Raises exposure: propranolol and theophylline AUC/Cmax increased after a single 20 mg piperine dose; phenytoin AUC/Cmax increased in volunteers and epileptic patients.

sources.citation: Bano G et al. Effect of piperine on bioavailability and pharmacokinetics of propranolol and theophylline in healthy volunteers. Eur J Clin Pharmacol 1991
Velpandian T et al. Piperine in food: interference in the pharmacokinetics of phenytoin. Eur J Drug Metab Pharmacokinet 2001
Pattanaik S et al. Effect of piperine on the steady-state pharmacokinetics of phenytoin in patients with epilepsy. Phytother Res 2006

interactions.notes: Doses studied (~20 mg piperine) exceed ordinary culinary intake; 'bioavailability enhancer' supplements deliver these doses.

agents: CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein substrates (digoxin, cyclosporine, verapamil etc.)
interactions.mechanism: Direct inhibition of human P-gp (Caco-2 digoxin/cyclosporine transport) and CYP3A4 (human liver microsomes; verapamil metabolism).
interactions.direction: Raises exposure (predicted) of dual CYP3A4/P-gp substrates; inhibition is mixed-type at low-micromolar concentrations.
interactions.significance: theoretical-to-moderate (in vitro; supported by clinical studies of item 31)

sources.citation: Bhardwaj RK et al. Piperine, a major constituent of black pepper, inhibits human P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4. J Pharmacol Exp Ther 2002

interactions.notes: Some animal data suggest repeated piperine can INDUCE P-gp/CYP3A in the long run - direction may depend on single vs chronic dosing.

interactions.mechanism: Proposed: coumarin constituents (herniarin, umbelliferone) additive anticoagulant effect and/or CYP inhibition (in vitro CYP1A2/3A4) - mechanism unconfirmed.
interactions.direction: Raised INR and bleeding: 70-year-old woman on warfarin, INR ~7.9 with retroperitoneal and other haematomas after drinking chamomile tea (4-5 cups/day) and using chamomile lotion.

sources.citation: Segal R, Pilote L. Warfarin interaction with Matricaria chamomilla. CMAJ 2006

interactions.notes: Plant coumarins are not 4-hydroxycoumarin anticoagulants, so the 'chamomile contains coumarin' explanation is weak; treat as signal, not established.

interactions.mechanism: Mixed: inhibits intestinal CYP3A while inducing hepatic CYP3A; inhibits CYP1A2.
interactions.direction: Oral midazolam: net small change (intestinal inhibition offsets hepatic induction); IV midazolam clearance increased 34%, AUC down 23%; caffeine (CYP1A2) exposure raised. Penzak 2010: CYP3A induced but lopinavir/ritonavir exposure unchanged (ritonavir's inhibition dominates).

sources.citation: Gorski JC et al. The effect of echinacea (Echinacea purpurea root) on cytochrome P450 activity in vivo. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2004
Penzak SR et al. Echinacea purpurea significantly induces cytochrome P450 3A activity but does not alter lopinavir-ritonavir exposure in healthy subjects. Pharmacotherapy 2010

interactions.notes: Good example that 'inhibitor' vs 'inducer' depends on tissue site and route of the victim drug.

interactions.mechanism: CBD inhibits CYP2C19 (and CYP3A4), blocking clearance of the active metabolite N-desmethylclobazam (nCLB, cleared by CYP2C19).
interactions.direction: Raises clobazam levels (~60%) and N-desmethylclobazam markedly (~500%) at 4 weeks, causing sedation; clobazam dose reduced in 77% of children.

sources.citation: Geffrey AL et al. Drug-drug interaction between clobazam and cannabidiol in children with refractory epilepsy. Epilepsia 2015

interactions.notes: Part of CBD's apparent anti-seizure benefit in early studies may reflect raised nCLB. Bidirectional: clobazam also raises CBD's active 7-OH metabolite.

interactions.mechanism: CBD inhibits CYP2C9 (S-warfarin) and CYP3A4.
interactions.direction: Raises warfarin effect (INR rose as CBD dose was escalated; warfarin dose had to be reduced ~30%).

sources.citation: Grayson L et al. An interaction between warfarin and cannabidiol, a case report. Epilepsy Behav Case Rep 2018

interactions.notes: Monitor INR when starting/increasing CBD; high-dose (Epidiolex-range) CBD is the main concern, low-dose retail CBD less clear.

interactions.mechanism: Pharmacodynamic/hepatotoxic synergy, not a PK change (valproate levels are not raised); mechanism unclear (mitochondrial/hepatocellular stress).
interactions.direction: Additive hepatotoxicity: transaminase (ALT/AST) elevations >3x ULN occur predominantly in patients co-treated with valproate; risk also rises with CBD dose and clobazam.

sources.citation: Devinsky O et al. Trial of Cannabidiol for Drug-Resistant Seizures in the Dravet Syndrome. N Engl J Med 2017
Lakhani VV et al. Assessing Liver Effects of Cannabidiol and Valproate Alone and in Combination Using Quantitative Systems Toxicology. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2023
EPIDIOLEX (cannabidiol) oral solution, US prescribing information, Warnings and Precautions 5.1 Hepatocellular Injury (label URL not fetched/verified)

interactions.notes: Label advises baseline and periodic LFTs, and consideration of valproate/CBD dose reduction if transaminases rise. Note PubMed also lists a duplicate/erratum record (PMID 28813226) for the Devinsky 2017 trial.

agents: cannabis or tobacco SMOKE (polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons)
CYP1A2 substrates: clozapine, olanzapine, theophylline, caffeine
interactions.mechanism: PAHs in smoke activate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor -> CYP1A2 induction. Due to combustion products, not THC/CBD/nicotine.
interactions.direction: Smoking LOWERS clozapine/olanzapine levels; QUITTING (or switching to edibles/vaping/patches) RAISES levels by roughly 30-50%+ within 1-2 weeks -> clozapine/olanzapine toxicity (sedation, seizures).
interactions.evidence: case reports + PK studies (largely tobacco; cannabis by same mechanism and case report)

sources.citation: Zullino DF et al. Tobacco and cannabis smoking cessation can lead to intoxication with clozapine or olanzapine. Int Clin Psychopharmacol 2002
Jusko WJ. Influence of cigarette smoking on drug metabolism in man. Drug Metab Rev 1979
Lowe EJ, Ackman ML. Impact of tobacco smoking cessation on stable clozapine or olanzapine treatment. Ann Pharmacother 2010

interactions.notes: Hazard is at CHANGE in smoking status (e.g. hospital admission, entering a smoke-free retreat). Nicotine replacement does not maintain induction. Marijuana smoking also increases theophylline clearance (Jusko 1978/79 data).

interactions.mechanism: Potent CYP1A2 inhibition by fluvoxamine (also CYP2C19); caffeine is ~95% CYP1A2-cleared.
interactions.direction: Raises caffeine exposure: total clearance fell ~80% (107 -> 21 mL/min), half-life 5 -> 31 h. Even 10-20 mg/day fluvoxamine inhibits CYP1A2.

sources.citation: Jeppesen U et al. A fluvoxamine-caffeine interaction study. Pharmacogenetics 1996
Christensen M et al. Low daily 10-mg and 20-mg doses of fluvoxamine inhibit the metabolism of both caffeine (CYP1A2) and omeprazole (CYP2C19). Clin Pharmacol Ther 2002

interactions.notes: Caffeine accumulates over days; advise cutting caffeine substantially. Same fluvoxamine mechanism makes tizanidine, theophylline, clozapine and melatonin levels soar.

interactions.mechanism: Quinolone inhibition of CYP1A2-mediated caffeine N-demethylation.
interactions.direction: Raises caffeine exposure: clearance reduced (~30-50% with ciprofloxacin, dose-dependent; enoxacin much stronger), half-life prolonged.
interactions.evidence: clinical trials + in vitro (human liver microsomes)

sources.citation: Healy DP et al. Interaction between oral ciprofloxacin and caffeine in normal volunteers. Antimicrob Agents Chemother 1989
Harder S et al. Ciprofloxacin-caffeine: a drug interaction established using in vivo and in vitro investigations. Am J Med 1989
Fuhr U et al. Quinolone inhibition of cytochrome P-450-dependent caffeine metabolism in human liver microsomes. Drug Metab Dispos 1990

interactions.notes: Clinically mostly jitteriness/insomnia; the same mechanism matters more for theophylline and tizanidine.

interactions.mechanism: Competitive inhibition of CYP1A2 by caffeine (both are CYP1A2 substrates).
interactions.direction: Raises clozapine exposure: controlled study ~19% AUC increase (14% lower clearance) in healthy volunteers; in patients, removing caffeine from the diet lowered clozapine levels by ~47%.
interactions.significance: moderate (larger in heavy coffee drinkers; sudden changes in intake matter)
interactions.evidence: clinical trial + patient withdrawal study + case reports

sources.citation: Hagg S et al. Effect of caffeine on clozapine pharmacokinetics in healthy volunteers. Br J Clin Pharmacol 2000
Carrillo JA et al. Effects of caffeine withdrawal from the diet on the metabolism of clozapine in schizophrenic patients. J Clin Psychopharmacol 1998
Carrillo JA, Benitez J. Clinically significant pharmacokinetic interactions between dietary caffeine and medications. Clin Pharmacokinet 2000

interactions.notes: Effect size differs a lot between the healthy-volunteer study (modest) and patients with high habitual intake (large). Keep caffeine intake stable.

agents: common ink cap mushroom (Coprinopsis atramentaria, formerly Coprinus atramentarius; coprine)
interactions.mechanism: Coprine is metabolised to 1-aminocyclopropanol, which inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) -> acetaldehyde accumulation (disulfiram-like).
interactions.direction: Disulfiram-like reaction when alcohol is taken from ~30 min up to ~72 h after eating the mushroom: flushing, palpitations, tachycardia, nausea/vomiting, hypotension.

sources.citation: Carlsson A et al. On the disulfiram-like effect of coprine, the pharmacologically active principle of Coprinus atramentarius. Acta Pharmacol Toxicol 1978
Tottmar O, Lindberg P. Effects on rat liver acetaldehyde dehydrogenases in vitro and in vivo by coprine, the disulfiram-like constituent of Coprinus atramentarius. Acta Pharmacol Toxicol 1977
Michelot D. Poisoning by Coprinus atramentarius. Nat Toxins 1992

interactions.notes: The mushroom is harmless without alcohol. Shaggy ink cap (Coprinus comatus) does not contain meaningful coprine. Coprine-like syndromes also reported with other species (e.g. Lepiota aspera, PMID 21370948).

interactions.mechanism: Traditionally claimed ALDH inhibition (disulfiram-like); controlled evidence does not support raised acetaldehyde. Alternative explanations: coincident adverse effects of either drug alone, metronidazole's own GI side effects, or a serotonergic/other mechanism (rat data).
interactions.direction: Classic claim: flushing, nausea, vomiting, tachycardia. RCT: metronidazole did NOT raise blood acetaldehyde or cause objective/subjective reactions with ethanol.
interactions.significance: minor-to-moderate / disputed (label warnings still advise avoiding alcohol during and 72 h after therapy)
interactions.evidence: RCT (negative) + literature review + scattered case reports

sources.citation: Williams CS, Woodcock KR. Do ethanol and metronidazole interact to produce a disulfiram-like reaction? Ann Pharmacother 2000
Visapaa JP et al. Lack of disulfiram-like reaction with metronidazole and ethanol. Ann Pharmacother 2002
Karamanakos PN et al. Pharmaceutical agents known to produce disulfiram-like reaction: effects on hepatic ethanol metabolism and brain monoamines. Int J Toxicol 2007

interactions.notes: CORRECTION: the 'metronidazole + alcohol = disulfiram reaction' teaching rests on weak 1960s-era case reports; Williams 2000 found the case evidence insufficient and Visapaa 2002 found no reaction in a double-blind trial. Caveat: Visapaa used healthy men and modest doses; individual reactions cannot be excluded, and colonic acetaldehyde changes have been reported (PMID 12107032).

interactions.mechanism: Coumarin hepatotoxicity in a susceptible subset of humans; coumarin cleared mainly by CYP2A6 7-hydroxylation, with the minor 3,4-epoxidation pathway producing hepatotoxic o-hydroxyphenylacetaldehyde.
interactions.direction: Dose-dependent rise in liver-injury risk (reversible transaminase elevations) when intake exceeds the TDI.
interactions.evidence: human data (coumarin-as-drug case series), human crossover PK, risk assessment

sources.citation: Abraham K et al. Toxicology and risk assessment of coumarin: focus on human data. Mol Nutr Food Res 2010
Abraham K et al. Relative bioavailability of coumarin from cinnamon and cinnamon-containing foods compared to isolated coumarin: a four-way crossover study in human volunteers. Mol Nutr Food Res 2011
Woehrlin F et al. Quantification of flavoring constituents in cinnamon: high variation of coumarin in cassia bark from the German retail market. J Agric Food Chem 2010

interactions.notes: TDI 0.1 mg/kg bw/day (BfR, confirming EFSA 2008), so about 6 mg/day for a 60 kg adult. Cassia coumarin content varies widely (Woehrlin: roughly 2-10 g/kg), so about 1-2 g (half to one teaspoon) of cassia a day can reach the TDI. Ceylon cinnamon (C. verum) has only trace coumarin. Coumarin from cassia powder is absorbed almost as well as the isolated compound (Abraham 2011). Daily cassia 'blood-sugar' capsule regimens are the main overexposure route.

agents: hepatotoxic drugs (acetaminophen, methotrexate, isoniazid, azoles, valproate, etc.)
interactions.mechanism: Additive hepatotoxic load. People with low CYP2A6 activity (CYP2A6*4/*2 alleles, or CYP2A6 inhibitors such as methoxsalen or tranylcypromine) shunt more coumarin to the 3,4-epoxide pathway.
interactions.direction: Additive liver-injury risk; CYP2A6 inhibition raises the fraction going down the toxic pathway.
interactions.evidence: mechanistic/in vitro + extrapolation from human coumarin hepatotoxicity

sources.citation: Lake BG. Coumarin metabolism, toxicity and carcinogenicity: relevance for human risk assessment. Food Chem Toxicol 1999
Abraham K et al. Toxicology and risk assessment of coumarin: focus on human data. Mol Nutr Food Res 2010

interactions.notes: CORRECTION: coumarin itself is NOT an anticoagulant and does not interact with warfarin through the vitamin-K mechanism. Dicoumarol (from spoiled sweet clover) and the warfarin family are 4-hydroxycoumarins. The concern with coumarin is the liver, not bleeding. No clinical drug-combination studies exist.

agents: green tea / green tea extract (EGCG, catechins)
interactions.mechanism: Green tea catechins inhibit intestinal OATP1A2 uptake of nadolol. Separately, concentrated EGCG extracts cause idiosyncratic hepatocellular DILI, which is worse with fasting bolus dosing.
interactions.direction: Green tea LOWERS nadolol exposure (Cmax and AUC each down about 85%) and blunts its BP-lowering effect. Extracts raise the risk of liver injury.
interactions.evidence: clinical PK trial (healthy volunteers); systematic review of DILI cases

sources.citation: Misaka S et al. Green tea ingestion greatly reduces plasma concentrations of nadolol in healthy subjects. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2014
Oketch-Rabah HA et al. United States Pharmacopeia (USP) comprehensive review of the hepatotoxicity of green tea extracts. Toxicol Rep 2020
Misaka S et al. Exposure of fexofenadine, but not pseudoephedrine, is markedly decreased by green tea extract in healthy volunteers. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2022

interactions.notes: The interaction came from brewed green tea (700 mL/day), not just extracts. Other OATP substrates (fexofenadine, also shown by Misaka 2022) are affected the same way. EFSA (2018) found that 800 mg/day or more EGCG from supplements raises transaminases. Brewed tea as a beverage is not the hepatotoxicity concern.

interactions.mechanism: Vitamin K1 is present in dried tea leaf, plus possible antiplatelet catechin effects.
interactions.direction: Antagonism: lower INR, reported with very high intake.

sources.citation: Taylor JR, Wilt VM. Probable antagonism of warfarin by green tea. Ann Pharmacother 1999

interactions.notes: CORRECTION/nuance: brewed green tea contains very little vitamin K because K1 is fat-soluble and barely extracts into water. The case involved roughly half a gallon to a gallon a day. Ordinary consistent intake is not a problem, while matcha (whole leaf eaten) or large changes in intake could be.

agents: vitamin K1-rich leafy greens (kale, spinach, collards, chard, parsley, natto=K2)
interactions.mechanism: Pharmacodynamic: dietary vitamin K bypasses VKORC1 inhibition by supplying reduced vitamin K for gamma-carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX, X.
interactions.direction: Sudden increases lower INR (clot risk); sudden decreases raise INR (bleeding risk).

sources.citation: Franco V et al. Role of dietary vitamin K intake in chronic oral anticoagulation: prospective evidence from observational and randomized protocols. Am J Med 2004
Boonyawat K et al. The effect of low-dose oral vitamin K supplementation on INR stability in patients receiving warfarin. A randomised trial. Thromb Haemost 2016

interactions.notes: CORRECTION of the popular advice: the rule is consistency, not avoidance. Patients told to cut out greens end up with low, unstable vitamin K status and less stable INRs. Natto (K2, menaquinone-7) is especially potent and long-acting. DOACs are unaffected.

interactions.mechanism: Proposed CYP2C9 inhibition is NOT supported in vivo. A possible minor pharmacodynamic effect (salicylic acid content, flavonoids).
interactions.direction: Possible small INR increase. Controlled trials show no PK change.
interactions.evidence: RCTs and PK studies (mostly null) + case reports (UK MHRA 2003-04 warnings)

sources.citation: Lilja JJ et al. Effects of daily ingestion of cranberry juice on the pharmacokinetics of warfarin, tizanidine, and midazolam. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2007
Ansell J et al. The absence of an interaction between warfarin and cranberry juice: a randomized, double-blind trial. J Clin Pharmacol 2009
Mohammed Abdul MI et al. Pharmacodynamic interaction of warfarin with cranberry but not with garlic in healthy subjects. Br J Pharmacol 2008

interactions.notes: CORRECTION: the widely repeated 'cranberry inhibits CYP2C9' claim is refuted (Lilja 2007: no change in S-warfarin AUC; Ansell 2009: no PK effect, and the one-day INR blip was judged likely chance). Mohammed Abdul 2008 found a modest pharmacodynamic INR increase using concentrated capsules. Sensible practice is INR monitoring if large amounts are started or stopped.

interactions.mechanism: In vitro CYP2C9 (and CYP3A) inhibition that did NOT translate to humans (no change in flurbiprofen clearance).
interactions.direction: Case reports describe raised INR while drinking and a subtherapeutic INR after stopping. The mechanism is unconfirmed.
interactions.evidence: in vitro + clinical PK (null) + 2 case reports

sources.citation: Hanley MJ et al. Pomegranate juice and pomegranate extract do not impair oral clearance of flurbiprofen in human volunteers: divergence from in vitro results. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2012
Komperda KE. Potential interaction between pomegranate juice and warfarin. Pharmacotherapy 2009
Jarvis S et al. Possible interaction between pomegranate juice and warfarin. Emerg Med J 2010

interactions.notes: CORRECTION: 'pomegranate is like grapefruit / a CYP2C9 inhibitor' is an in-vitro artifact. Human CYP2C9 probe data are null. Keep it as a 'monitor INR on big diet changes' item.

agents: American ginseng (Panax quinquefolius); Asian ginseng (P. ginseng)
interactions.mechanism: Unclear; possible induction of warfarin metabolism or a pharmacodynamic effect. Ginsenosides also have in-vitro antiplatelet activity.
interactions.direction: LOWERS warfarin effect: INR and plasma warfarin both decreased vs placebo.
interactions.evidence: RCT in healthy volunteers + case reports

sources.citation: Yuan CS et al. Brief communication: American ginseng reduces warfarin's effect in healthy patients: a randomized, controlled trial. Ann Intern Med 2004

interactions.notes: CORRECTION to the prompt: Yuan 2004 tested AMERICAN ginseng (P. quinquefolius), not Panax ginseng (Asian/Korean). Data for Asian ginseng are case reports plus mixed small trials, and some trials found no effect. Direction is reduced anticoagulation (clot risk), the opposite of the 'herbs thin blood' assumption.

interactions.mechanism: Unknown; possibly additive CNS stimulation or monoaminergic effects.
interactions.direction: Additive adverse effects: headache, insomnia, tremor, irritability/manic-like symptoms.

sources.citation: Jones BD, Runikis AM. Interaction of ginseng with phenelzine. J Clin Psychopharmacol 1987
Shader RI, Greenblatt DJ. Phenelzine and the dream machine--ramblings and reflections. J Clin Psychopharmacol 1985 (ginseng/bee pollen case; PMID not confirmed)

interactions.notes: No hypertensive crisis has been documented. The reported events are stimulant/manic-type.

interactions.mechanism: Unknown. Contains coumarin derivatives (e.g., osthole) and ferulic acid with antiplatelet activity. Rabbit data show a pharmacodynamic but not a pharmacokinetic effect.
interactions.direction: Raises INR / bleeding risk.

sources.citation: Page RL 2nd, Lawrence JD. Potentiation of warfarin by dong quai. Pharmacotherapy 1999
Lo AC et al. Danggui (Angelica sinensis) affects the pharmacodynamics but not the pharmacokinetics of warfarin in rabbits. Eur J Drug Metab Pharmacokinet 1995

interactions.notes: The case showed INR more than doubled after 4 weeks, normalising 1 month after stopping.

interactions.mechanism: Proposed: coumarin-type constituents and antiplatelet effects. The mechanism is unproven.
interactions.direction: Raises INR (case with boldo+fenugreek, positive rechallenge).

sources.citation: Lambert JP, Cormier J. Potential interaction between warfarin and boldo-fenugreek. Pharmacotherapy 2001

interactions.notes: Confounded by the boldo co-ingestion. Fenugreek also lowers glucose, so watch additive hypoglycaemia with antidiabetics.

interactions.mechanism: Idiosyncratic cholestatic/mixed DILI. Separately, it raises thyroid hormone (T4/T3), with case reports of thyrotoxicosis and painless thyroiditis.
interactions.direction: Liver injury after 2-12 week latency. May raise thyroid hormones, which adds to levothyroxine and opposes antithyroid therapy.
interactions.evidence: DILIN case series + case reports; small RCT thyroid signal

sources.citation: Björnsson HK et al. Ashwagandha-induced liver injury: a case series from Iceland and the US Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network. Liver Int 2020
Kamal HI et al. Ashwagandha as a unique cause of thyrotoxicosis presenting with supraventricular tachycardia. Cureus 2022
Gannon JM et al. Subtle changes in thyroid indices during a placebo-controlled study of an extract of Withania somnifera in persons with bipolar disorder. J Ayurveda Integr Med 2014

interactions.notes: LiverTox lists ashwagandha as a recognised cause of cholestatic hepatitis. It also has sedative GABAergic activity, so it may add to benzodiazepines and other CNS depressants. Several EU states (e.g., Denmark 2023) restricted ashwagandha supplements.
interactions.type: toxicity (agent alone or with liver/CNS load)

agents: CNS depressants (benzodiazepines, alcohol, opioids, Z-drugs, barbiturates)
interactions.mechanism: Pharmacodynamic GABAergic additivity (valerenic acid is a GABA-A modulator). Minimal CYP effect.
interactions.direction: Additive sedation/psychomotor impairment. No meaningful PK change for CYP3A4/2D6 substrates.

sources.citation: Donovan JL et al. Multiple night-time doses of valerian had minimal effects on CYP3A4 activity and no effect on CYP2D6 activity in healthy volunteers. Drug Metab Dispos 2004
Carrasco MC et al. Interactions of Valeriana officinalis L. and Passiflora incarnata L. in a patient treated with lorazepam. Phytother Res 2009

interactions.notes: In Donovan, alprazolam Cmax rose modestly (~19%) and was not otherwise significant. The risk is additive sedation, not metabolic.

interactions.mechanism: Pharmacodynamic additive CNS depression (GABAergic; hops 2-methyl-3-buten-2-ol).
interactions.direction: Additive sedation.

sources.citation: Carrasco MC et al. Interactions of Valeriana officinalis L. and Passiflora incarnata L. in a patient treated with lorazepam. Phytother Res 2009

interactions.notes: The case was valerian + passionflower + lorazepam (dizziness, tremor, fatigue). No human data on hops specifically. Caution is greatest with driving and with combined opioid/alcohol use.

interactions.mechanism: Alpha-2 adrenoceptor antagonist that increases central and peripheral noradrenaline release. With MAOIs or other sympathomimetics it adds to pressor load.
interactions.direction: Raises BP and HR, with risk of hypertensive crisis. Opposes clonidine and other antihypertensives.

sources.citation: Tam SW et al. Yohimbine: a clinical review. Pharmacol Ther 2001
Ruck B et al. Hypertensive crisis from herbal treatment of impotence. Am J Emerg Med 1999

interactions.notes: CORRECTION: yohimbe is often labelled 'an MAOI'. Its MAO-inhibiting activity is weak and of unclear relevance, and the main risk is alpha-2 blockade (anxiety, panic, hypertension). Commercial 'yohimbe' products often have unpredictable yohimbine content.

interactions.mechanism: Pharmacodynamic sympathomimetic synergy: ephedrine (indirect/direct adrenergic agonist) plus caffeine (adenosine antagonism, PDE inhibition).
interactions.direction: Additive/synergistic rises in BP, HR and arrhythmia risk. Reports of stroke, MI, seizure and sudden death.
interactions.evidence: adverse event series (FDA MedWatch review) + RAND meta-analysis of RCTs

sources.citation: Haller CA, Benowitz NL. Adverse cardiovascular and central nervous system events associated with dietary supplements containing ephedra alkaloids. N Engl J Med 2000
Shekelle PG et al. Efficacy and safety of ephedra and ephedrine for weight loss and athletic performance: a meta-analysis. JAMA 2003
FDA. Final rule declaring dietary supplements containing ephedrine alkaloids adulterated (69 FR 6788, Feb 11 2004; effective Apr 12 2004)

interactions.notes: Shekelle: modest weight loss (~0.9 kg/month), with 2.2-3.6-fold higher odds of psychiatric, autonomic, GI symptoms and palpitations. The FDA ban covers supplements only. Traditional Chinese medicine teas and OTC ephedrine (pseudoephedrine products) are regulated separately. MAOIs make ephedrine much more dangerous.

interactions.mechanism: p-Synephrine has weak alpha-1 and beta-3 adrenergic activity (much weaker than m-synephrine/phenylephrine or ephedrine). Pressor effects in products mainly come from caffeine and co-stimulants.
interactions.direction: In controlled trials p-synephrine up to ~100 mg did not augment the BP/HR effects of caffeine. Multi-ingredient 'ephedra-free' products raised BP/HR.
interactions.evidence: RCT crossover + case reports + in vivo CYP phenotyping

sources.citation: Ratamess NA et al. Acute cardiovascular effects of bitter orange extract (p-synephrine) consumed alone and in combination with caffeine in human subjects. Phytother Res 2018
Haller CA et al. Hemodynamic effects of ephedra-free weight-loss supplements in humans. Am J Med 2005
Gurley BJ et al. In vivo assessment of botanical supplementation on human cytochrome P450 phenotypes: Citrus aurantium, Echinacea, milk thistle, saw palmetto. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2004

interactions.notes: CORRECTION/nuance: 'bitter orange is the new ephedra' is overstated for p-synephrine alone. Haller 2005 found an 8-fold higher synephrine-only dose had no BP effect, and effects tracked caffeine. Case reports of cardiac events exist, but products are often adulterated or multi-stimulant. Bitter orange juice (furanocoumarins) can inhibit gut CYP3A like grapefruit, while extract capsules did not in Gurley 2004.

agents: CYP3A substrates; CYP2D6 substrates; opioids, benzodiazepines, alcohol, other CNS depressants
interactions.mechanism: PK: mitragynine strongly inhibits CYP2D6 and CYP3A in vitro. In humans kratom tea modestly inhibits intestinal CYP3A and has no measurable CYP2D6 effect. PD: mu-opioid partial agonism adds to respiratory depression from other depressants.
interactions.direction: Raises midazolam AUC 1.39x and Cmax 1.50x (CYP3A). Dextromethorphan (2D6) is unchanged. Additive CNS/respiratory depression with opioids and sedatives.
interactions.evidence: clinical PK trial + CDC death surveillance + forensic case series

sources.citation: Tanna RS et al. Clinical assessment of the drug interaction potential of the psychotropic natural product kratom. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2023
Olsen EO et al. Notes from the Field: Unintentional drug overdose deaths with kratom detected - 27 States, July 2016-December 2017. MMWR 2019
Kronstrand R et al. Unintentional fatal intoxications with mitragynine and O-desmethyltramadol from the herbal blend Krypton. J Anal Toxicol 2011

interactions.notes: CORRECTION: the strong in-vitro CYP2D6 inhibition did NOT show up clinically (dextromethorphan AUC ratio ~0.99). CYP3A is the relevant pathway (also substrate: itraconazole raises mitragynine, Mongar 2024, PMID 38481700). In the CDC data kratom was detected in 152 of ~27,000 overdose deaths and was the sole substance in only 7, with fentanyl/heroin co-present in most. The Swedish 'Krypton' deaths involved kratom adulterated with O-desmethyltramadol. Concentrated 7-OH-mitragynine products are a newer, more potent risk.

interactions.mechanism: Pharmacodynamic: arecoline is a muscarinic agonist that antagonises anticholinergic anti-EPS drugs and adds cholinergic tone.
interactions.direction: Precipitates extrapyramidal symptoms (rigidity, tremor, akathisia) in patients on depot neuroleptics.

sources.citation: Deahl M. Betel nut-induced extrapyramidal syndrome: an unusual drug interaction. Mov Disord 1989

interactions.notes: Arecoline is also a partial nicotinic agonist and areca has MAO-inhibitory/tyramine-pressor effects in rodents (Khan 2014, PMID 24577919). Areca is an IARC Group 1 carcinogen.

interactions.mechanism: Myristicin showed weak MAO inhibition in rodent tissue (1963). Clinical relevance is unestablished.
interactions.direction: Theoretical additive MAO inhibition or serotonergic effect.
interactions.evidence: animal (1963) + toxicology case reports of nutmeg intoxication alone

sources.citation: Truitt EB Jr et al. Evidence of monoamine oxidase inhibition by myristicin and nutmeg. Proc Soc Exp Biol Med 1963
Ichibayashi R et al. Nutmeg poisoning with electrolyte abnormalities: a case report. Cureus 2024

interactions.notes: No human case of a nutmeg-MAOI interaction is documented. Nutmeg intoxication (typically 2 tablespoons/10-30 g or more) produces an anticholinergic-like picture with tachycardia, nausea, agitation and delayed onset of 3-8 h lasting 24-48 h. The amounts used in cooking are irrelevant.

agents: MAOIs (nonselective: phenelzine, tranylcypromine, isocarboxazid; also linezolid)
interactions.mechanism: L-DOPA is converted to dopamine and noradrenaline. With MAO-A blocked, catecholamine breakdown is prevented, leading to pressor crisis.
interactions.direction: Hypertensive crisis (raised BP, flushing, palpitations).
interactions.evidence: clinical report (1970) + mechanistic + Mucuna PK RCT

sources.citation: Hunter KR et al. Monoamine oxidase inhibitors and L-dopa. Br Med J 1970
Katzenschlager R et al. Mucuna pruriens in Parkinson's disease: a double blind clinical and pharmacological study. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2004
Gillman PK. Advances pertaining to the pharmacology and interactions of irreversible nonselective monoamine oxidase inhibitors. J Clin Psychopharmacol 2011

interactions.notes: Levodopa labels contraindicate nonselective MAOIs (stop at least 2 weeks before). Selective MAO-B inhibitors (selegiline, rasagiline, safinamide) are routinely co-prescribed with L-DOPA at labelled doses. Mucuna L-DOPA content is variable. In Katzenschlager, 30 g Mucuna produced L-dopa AUC about 165% larger than 200/50 LD/CD, so it is potent and dose-equivalence is non-trivial. Harmala/ayahuasca MAOIs (reversible MAO-A) carry the same theoretical concern.

interactions.mechanism: 5-HTP bypasses rate-limiting tryptophan hydroxylase and is decarboxylated to serotonin, adding to reuptake/MAO blockade (serotonin toxicity). Carbidopa inhibits peripheral AADC, raising systemic 5-HTP levels.
interactions.direction: Additive serotonergic toxicity. Carbidopa raises 5-HTP exposure; the combination has been linked to scleroderma-like illness.
interactions.evidence: case reports (scleroderma with carbidopa) + mechanism + veterinary toxicity data

sources.citation: Joly P et al. Development of pseudobullous morphea and scleroderma-like illness during therapy with L-5-hydroxytryptophan and carbidopa. J Am Acad Dermatol 1991
Auffranc JC et al. Sclerodermiform and poikilodermal syndrome observed during treatment with carbidopa and 5-hydroxytryptophan. Ann Dermatol Venereol 1985

interactions.notes: Published human cases of serotonin syndrome from 5-HTP + SSRI alone are surprisingly sparse. The risk is mechanistically strong and best documented for tryptophan + MAOI (entry 66). Dog ingestions of 5-HTP tablets cause severe serotonin toxicity. The 'Peak X' contaminant linked to eosinophilia-myalgia was reported in some 5-HTP lots.

interactions.mechanism: Precursor loading plus MAO-A blockade leads to excess serotonin.
interactions.direction: Serotonin toxicity (hyperreflexia, myoclonus, confusion, hyperthermia).

sources.citation: Thomas JM, Rubin EH. Case report of a toxic reaction from a combination of tryptophan and phenelzine. Am J Psychiatry 1984
Pope HG Jr et al. Toxic reactions to the combination of monoamine oxidase inhibitors and tryptophan. Am J Psychiatry 1985

interactions.notes: Tryptophan was historically used (under supervision) to augment MAOIs, so toxicity is dose-dependent rather than universal. Dietary tryptophan (turkey etc.) is not the issue. Supplement-level grams are.

interactions.mechanism: SAMe is a methyl donor in monoamine synthesis and has antidepressant serotonergic effects, adding to serotonergic drugs.
interactions.direction: Serotonin toxicity (case with clomipramine).

sources.citation: Iruela LM et al. Toxic interaction of S-adenosylmethionine and clomipramine. Am J Psychiatry 1993

interactions.notes: SAMe is also reported to trigger mania in bipolar disorder.

interactions.mechanism: In vitro MAO-A and MAO-B inhibition by root extracts.
interactions.direction: Theoretical additive serotonergic/MAO effect.

sources.citation: van Diermen D et al. Monoamine oxidase inhibition by Rhodiola rosea L. roots. J Ethnopharmacol 2009

interactions.notes: No human interaction cases are documented. In-vitro potency does not establish clinical MAO inhibition at supplement doses.

interactions.mechanism: In vitro CYP3A/2C9 and UGT inhibition. Human phenotyping shows no clinically relevant effect.
interactions.direction: No meaningful change for midazolam (3A), debrisoquine (2D6), caffeine (1A2) or chlorzoxazone (2E1).
interactions.evidence: multiple clinical phenotyping trials + systematic review

sources.citation: Gurley BJ et al. In vivo assessment of botanical supplementation on human cytochrome P450 phenotypes. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2004
Gurley B et al. Assessing the clinical significance of botanical supplementation on human CYP3A activity: milk thistle and black cohosh. J Clin Pharmacol 2006
Tvrdý V et al. Systematic review of pharmacokinetics and potential pharmacokinetic interactions of flavonolignans from silymarin. Med Res Rev 2021

interactions.notes: Possible small CYP2C9 effect (losartan, in CYP2C9*1/*1 subjects) and gut UGT inhibition in vitro. Otherwise one of the safest herbs interaction-wise. 'Liver detox' marketing does not imply induction.

interactions.mechanism: Inhibition of CYP2D6 (strongest), CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 after repeated dosing. Cyclosporine levels raised via CYP3A4 (and possibly P-gp).
interactions.direction: RAISES exposure of 2D6/2C9/3A4 substrates. Markedly raises cyclosporine blood concentrations.

sources.citation: Guo Y et al. Repeated administration of berberine inhibits cytochromes P450 in humans. Eur J Clin Pharmacol 2012
Wu X et al. Effects of berberine on the blood concentration of cyclosporin A in renal transplanted recipients: clinical and pharmacokinetic study. Eur J Clin Pharmacol 2005
Gurley BJ et al. Clinical assessment of CYP2D6-mediated herb-drug interactions in humans: goldenseal etc. Mol Nutr Food Res 2008

interactions.notes: Guo: 300 mg t.i.d. for 2 weeks (a common 'metabolic' supplement dose). Goldenseal inhibited CYP2D6 by about 50% (Gurley 2008). Relevant victims include dextromethorphan, codeine/tramadol (reduced activation), metoprolol, many antidepressants and antipsychotics, midazolam, and statins. Berberine also lowers glucose (additive with metformin and sulfonylureas).

agents: Schisandra (S. sphenanthera / Wuzhi tablet; S. chinensis)
interactions.mechanism: Lignans (schisantherin A, deoxyschizandrin) inhibit intestinal/hepatic CYP3A and P-gp.
interactions.direction: RAISES tacrolimus exposure substantially (oral bioavailability up).
interactions.evidence: clinical PK trial (healthy volunteers) + in vivo/in vitro mechanistic

sources.citation: Xin HW et al. Effects of Schisandra sphenanthera extract on the pharmacokinetics of tacrolimus in healthy volunteers. Br J Clin Pharmacol 2007
Qin XL et al. In vivo to in vitro effects of six bioactive lignans of Wuzhi tablet on the CYP3A/P-glycoprotein-mediated absorption and metabolism of tacrolimus. Drug Metab Dispos 2014
Qin XL et al. Effect of Tacrolimus on the pharmacokinetics of bioactive lignans of Wuzhi tablet and the potential roles of CYP3A and P-gp. Phytomedicine 2014

interactions.notes: Xin 2007: tacrolimus AUC up about 164% and Cmax about 227%. In China, Wuzhi tablet is deliberately co-prescribed to spare tacrolimus dose. Uncontrolled self-use risks nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity. Also expect raised midazolam, cyclosporine, etc.

agents: CYP3A4, CYP2D6, CYP2C9 substrates; CYP1A2 substrates
interactions.mechanism: At 1 g/day for 4 weeks: inhibits CYP3A4, CYP2D6, CYP2C9 and induces CYP1A2 (phenotyping cocktail).
interactions.direction: May raise exposure of 3A4/2D6/2C9 substrates and lower exposure of 1A2 substrates.

sources.citation: Chow HH et al. Resveratrol modulates drug- and carcinogen-metabolizing enzymes in a healthy volunteer study. Cancer Prev Res 2010

interactions.notes: Wine contains milligram amounts, irrelevant compared with the 1 g supplement dose. Resveratrol also has antiplatelet effects (warfarin/antiplatelet additivity, theoretical).

interactions.mechanism: Mixed: P-gp induction (Wang 2013) and OATP modulation lowering talinolol exposure. CYP2C9 and CYP2E1 inhibition in short human trials.
interactions.direction: Bidirectional and drug-specific: talinolol slightly LOWER, diclofenac and chlorzoxazone HIGHER.

sources.citation: Nguyen MA et al. Effect of single-dose and short-term administration of quercetin on the pharmacokinetics of talinolol in humans. Eur J Pharm Sci 2014
Wang SY et al. Effect of quercetin on P-glycoprotein transport ability in Chinese healthy subjects. Eur J Clin Nutr 2013
Bedada SK et al. Evaluation of the effect of quercetin treatment on CYP2C9 enzyme activity of diclofenac in healthy human volunteers. Phytother Res 2018

interactions.notes: CORRECTION: 'quercetin inhibits P-gp, so it raises drug levels' is not what human studies show for talinolol. It went down. Several of the positive CYP trials come from a single group with small samples. Treat as unpredictable and monitor narrow-index drugs.

agents: psyllium / high-fibre meals; also coffee, soy, calcium, iron
levothyroxine; also digoxin, lithium, carbamazepine, metformin (fibre binding)
interactions.mechanism: Physical adsorption/binding in gut and delayed gastric emptying. Calcium/iron/aluminium chelate T4.
interactions.direction: May lower or delay absorption.
interactions.significance: minor (psyllium for T4); moderate (calcium/iron/coffee for T4)
interactions.evidence: small clinical absorption study + systematic review

sources.citation: Chiu AC, Sherman SI. Effects of pharmacological fiber supplements on levothyroxine absorption. Thyroid 1998
Wiesner A et al. Levothyroxine interactions with food and dietary supplements - a systematic review. Pharmaceuticals 2021
Skelin M et al. Factors affecting gastrointestinal absorption of levothyroxine: a review. Clin Ther 2017

interactions.notes: CORRECTION: the popular 'psyllium blocks levothyroxine' claim is weak. Chiu 1998 found absorption 89% alone vs 80% with psyllium (not significant), with only a delay. Calcium carbonate, iron salts, coffee taken with the tablet, and PPIs are the better-documented culprits. Standard advice still applies: take T4 fasting and separate supplements by about 4 h.

agents: calcium/dairy (milk, yogurt), antacids, iron, zinc, magnesium
interactions.mechanism: Chelation of divalent/trivalent cations by the drug in the gut, forming non-absorbable complexes.
interactions.direction: LOWERS antibiotic absorption: milk/yogurt cut ciprofloxacin AUC by 30-36% and Cmax by 36-47%. Tetracycline loss is larger.

sources.citation: Neuvonen PJ et al. Interference of dairy products with the absorption of ciprofloxacin. Clin Pharmacol Ther 1991
Neuvonen PJ. Interactions with the absorption of tetracyclines. Drugs 1976

interactions.notes: Doxycycline and minocycline are less affected by dairy than tetracycline, but still strongly affected by iron and antacids. Separation: take the antibiotic 2 h before or 4-6 h after cation sources. Calcium-fortified juices count.

agents: grapefruit juice (naringin), also orange and apple juice
interactions.mechanism: Inhibition of intestinal OATP1A2 uptake transporter (not CYP3A).
interactions.direction: LOWERS fexofenadine exposure: AUC and Cmax reduced to about 30-40% of the water control.
interactions.evidence: clinical PK trial + in vitro transporter

sources.citation: Dresser GK et al. Fruit juices inhibit organic anion transporting polypeptide-mediated drug uptake to decrease the oral availability of fexofenadine. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2002
Greenblatt DJ. Analysis of drug interactions involving fruit beverages and organic anion-transporting polypeptides. J Clin Pharmacol 2009

interactions.notes: CORRECTION of the 'grapefruit always raises levels' heuristic: for OATP-uptake substrates the direction is reversed, giving reduced efficacy. The fexofenadine label advises taking it with water, not fruit juice. Effect wears off within about 4 h, unlike the CYP3A mechanism, which lasts more than 24 h.

agents: celiprolol; fexofenadine; aliskiren, atenolol, some others (OATP1A2/2B1 substrates)
interactions.mechanism: Intestinal OATP inhibition by juice flavonoids (hesperidin, phloridzin). Possible pH/complexation contribution.
interactions.direction: LOWERS exposure: orange juice cut celiprolol AUC by about 83%. Apple and orange juice lower fexofenadine.

sources.citation: Lilja JJ et al. Orange juice substantially reduces the bioavailability of the beta-adrenergic-blocking agent celiprolol. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2004
Dresser GK et al. Fruit juices inhibit OATP-mediated drug uptake to decrease the oral availability of fexofenadine. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2002
Chen M et al. Food-drug interactions precipitated by fruit juices other than grapefruit juice: an update review. J Food Drug Anal 2018

interactions.notes: Orange juice does not inhibit CYP3A the way grapefruit or Seville (bitter) orange juice does. Its effect is transport-mediated and lowers exposure.

interactions.mechanism: Chronic ethanol induces CYP2E1, increasing NAPQI formation, while depleting glutathione (malnutrition, fasting). Acute ethanol competitively inhibits CYP2E1 and is transiently protective.
interactions.direction: Increased hepatotoxicity at therapeutic-to-modestly-supratherapeutic acetaminophen doses in chronic drinkers.

sources.citation: Zimmerman HJ, Maddrey WC. Acetaminophen (paracetamol) hepatotoxicity with regular intake of alcohol: analysis of instances of therapeutic misadventure. Hepatology 1995

interactions.notes: CORRECTION/nuance: one drink plus a standard dose is not the classic danger. The danger is sustained heavy drinking, especially after stopping (induced enzyme, no competing ethanol) plus fasting. The US label warns against 3 or more drinks/day with acetaminophen. Many hepatologists cap chronic drinkers at about 2 g/day. NAC is the antidote.

interactions.mechanism: Pharmacodynamic additive/synergistic CNS and respiratory depression (GABA-A potentiation + mu-opioid brainstem depression). Ethanol may also raise some benzodiazepine levels acutely (CYP3A/2C19 inhibition).
interactions.direction: Synergistic respiratory depression, sedation and overdose death.
interactions.evidence: volunteer RCT (respiratory) + toxicology review + mortality data; FDA 2016 boxed warning

sources.citation: van der Schrier R et al. Influence of ethanol on oxycodone-induced respiratory depression: a dose-escalating study in young and elderly individuals. Anesthesiology 2017
Tanaka E. Toxicological interactions between alcohol and benzodiazepines. J Toxicol Clin Toxicol 2002
FDA Drug Safety Communication (Aug 2016): boxed warning on combined opioid + benzodiazepine use

interactions.notes: van der Schrier: about 1 g/L blood ethanol plus 20 mg oxycodone gave more ventilatory depression than either alone, and the elderly were more affected. Some extended-release opioid formulations show alcohol 'dose dumping' (the reason Palladone was withdrawn in 2005). Harm reduction: avoid combining, use lower doses, don't use alone, and have naloxone (which reverses only the opioid component).

interactions.mechanism: Metformin: ethanol inhibits hepatic gluconeogenesis and raises NADH/NAD+, increasing lactate production while reducing clearance, which adds to metformin's lactate burden (worse with binges, liver disease, dehydration). MAOI: tyramine in unpasteurised/draft beer (bacterial decarboxylation) is not deaminated by gut/liver MAO-A, triggering noradrenaline release and pressor crisis.
interactions.direction: Metformin + binge alcohol raises lactic acidosis and hypoglycaemia risk. MAOI + high-tyramine beer causes hypertensive crisis.
interactions.evidence: FDA label warnings + case reports + reviews; tyramine content surveys

sources.citation: See KC. Metformin-associated lactic acidosis: a mini review of pathophysiology, diagnosis and management in critically ill patients. World J Diabetes 2024
Miyata Y et al. Metformin-associated lactic acidosis induced by even modest amounts of alcohol: a case report. Cureus 2025
Van den Eynde V et al. The Prescriber's Guide to the MAOI Diet - Thinking Through Tyramine Troubles. Psychopharmacol Bull 2022
Gillman PK. Advances pertaining to the pharmacology and interactions of irreversible nonselective MAOIs. J Clin Psychopharmacol 2011

interactions.notes: CORRECTION: not all beer is high-tyramine. Mainstream bottled/canned pasteurised beers are generally low. Tap/draft, craft-unpasteurised and some Belgian/homebrew beers are the risk, and wine is usually low. verified_sources_applications.claim: Tisserand Institute general dilution guidelines (face 0.2-1.5%, body 1-5%, children by age, pregnancy ~1%).
verified_sources_applications.verified_value: General dilution guide (c Tisserand Institute 2022): facial cosmetics/deodorants 0.2-1.5% (common 1%); body oils & lotions 1-3% (common 2%); bath products 2-4% (3%); acne spot treatment/wounds 2-10% (4%); pain, 'feelgood' rollerballs 3-10% (5%). Children, from Essential Oil Safety 2e: 0-3 months 0.1-0.2%; 3-24 months 0.25-0.5%; 2-6 years 1-2%; 6-15 years 1.5-3%; 15+ years 2.5-5%. For under 6 the percentage applies to any topical application; for 6+ it is for full-body application, and local applications may be more concentrated. Diffusion: 30-60 min on, 30-60 min off; do not intensively inhale for more than 15-20 min; no undiluted drops in the bath. Pregnancy: the Tisserand Institute gives no percentage, only 'lower dilutions and avoiding some oils entirely'; the '1%' figure circulates on blogs and, where sourced, traces to Christie et al. 2013, not Tisserand.
